title: The Narrowing Profit Boom
gist: China's headline corporate profit rebound and its exit from roughly three years of producer-price deflation are almost entirely driven by three industries — coal, non-ferrous metals and chips — while most industries are still loss-making and deflating. Absent capacity expansion by those winners, which Gavekal thinks unlikely, the recovery stays a narrow pocket phenomenon rather than a broad industrial upcycle.

insights.claim: China's corporate profits are surging after several years of essentially no growth, marking a genuine turn in the aggregate earnings cycle.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The aggregate print supports the bullish China-reflation narrative, but the index level is the wrong unit of analysis — check breadth before adding broad China industrial exposure.
insights.quote: China's corporate profits are surging after years of little growth

insights.claim: Chinese producer prices are rising again after roughly three years of deflation, ending one of the longest PPI down-cycles of the post-2020 period.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A PPI inflection is the classic trigger for rotating into Chinese cyclicals and for repricing global goods-deflation assumptions — but only if it broadens beyond a few input-price lines.
insights.quote: producer prices are rising again following roughly three years of deflation
insights.locator: and producer prices are rising again

insights.claim: Despite improving headline figures, the majority of Chinese industries are still posting losses and still mired in deflation, so the aggregate profit and price recovery misrepresents the typical firm.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Fade the 'China reflation is here' read-through for broad industrials and downstream manufacturers; median-industry margins, not aggregates, are the honest gauge.
insights.quote: The majority of industries are still posting losses and mired in deflation.

insights.claim: Coal, non-ferrous metals and chips account for nearly all of the top-line gains in China's current profit upswing, making the recovery a three-sector story rather than an industrial-wide one.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Concentrate long exposure in Chinese coal, non-ferrous metal and semiconductor names; the rest of the industrial complex has no earnings support from this cycle.
insights.quote: coal, non-ferrous metals and chips account for nearly all the top-line gains
insights.locator: the current upswing rests on an unusually narrow set

insights.claim: Earnings cycles are always uneven, but the concentration in China's current upswing is unusually narrow even by that standard — a distinction that separates a normal cyclical recovery from a commodity- and chip-specific windfall.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Use breadth of profit gains, not the level, as the test for whether a Chinese industrial recovery is investable beyond a handful of sectors.
insights.quote: while every earnings cycle is uneven, the current upswing rests on an unusually narrow set of industries
insights.locator: And while every earnings cycle is uneven

insights.claim: The profit boom in China's winning industries can only spread to the rest of industry if those winners substantially expand production capacity, since their capex is the channel that would transmit their windfall into other sectors' revenues.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch capex and capacity announcements from Chinese coal, non-ferrous and semiconductor producers as the leading indicator for any broadening of the industrial recovery.
insights.locator: Unless those winners substantially expand their production capacity

insights.claim: Gavekal judges substantial capacity expansion by China's coal, non-ferrous metals and chip producers over the coming months to be unlikely, and therefore expects the profit boom to stay confined to a few pockets of the industrial sector.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Position for a persistently narrow China profit cycle: stay long the three winners, avoid broad industrial beta, and treat any big capacity announcement as the signal to change that stance.
insights.quote: the profit boom will probably remain concentrated in just a few pockets of the industrial sector
